- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.17) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-0.30) within 5 days, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 1–2% per negative sentiment unit.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >+10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.17), model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for latent momentum.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lag: if true outcome is below 30d forecast by >5%, adjust next forecast down by 1–2% to reflect recent downward momentum.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings (e.g., -0.22, -0.61), model tends to ignore trend; apply smoothing filter to dampen short-term volatility in forecast.
